{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script
#
# This is a self-submitting Flux script: run it directly (e.g., `./process_join_annotate_counts.flux.sh`).
# It will submit itself to Flux with the translated resource requests.

# Translated resources from Slurm:
#   -N 1        -> -N 1
#   -n 1        -> -n 1
#   -o ...      -> -o output=...
JOBID=$(flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -o output=log/process_join_annotate_counts.out --wrap "bash $0 __flux_inner")

echo "Submitted Flux job: $JOBID"

if [ "${1:-}" = "__flux_inner" ]; then
  # NOTE: Slurm --mem=16G not translated.
  # Performance implication: without a memory reservation/limit, the job may contend for memory or be OOM-killed, affecting reliability/performance.

  # NOTE: Slurm -e log/... not translated.
  # Performance implication: none; operational implication: stderr will follow Flux defaults unless configured at submission.

  # NOTE: Slurm --mail-type=BEGIN,END,FAIL not translated.
  # Performance implication: none; operational implication: no email notifications.

  eval $(spack load --sh miniconda3)
  source activate active-learning

  flux run -n 1 python3 src/process_and_join_counts.py
  flux run -n 1 python3 src/annotate_data.py
fi
"
}

No time limit (`-t`) is requested in Flux; the job will run with the system/default time limit, which may differ from the original Slurm defaults (resource limit concern).
No memory limit/reservation is requested in Flux (Slurm `--mem=16G` was omitted), so the job will run with default memory policy, which may differ from the original resource intent.
